    # Find groups with outlier percentage > 15%
    group_pct = df.groupby(level)['is_outlier'].mean() * 100
    high_outlier_groups = group_pct[group_pct > 15].index.tolist()
    
    if high_outlier_groups:
        print(f"\n{level} groups with >15% outlier rate:")
        
        for group in high_outlier_groups[:3]:  # Limit to top 3
            group_data = df[df[level] == group]
            group_outliers = group_data[group_data['is_outlier']]
            group_inliers = group_data[~group_data['is_outlier']]
            
            outlier_pct = (len(group_outliers) / len(group_data) * 100)
            print(f"\n  {level} '{group}': {len(group_outliers)} outliers ({outlier_pct:.1f}%)")
            
            # Find most distinctive attributes
            distinctive_attrs = []
            for col in numeric_cols:
                if col in group_data.columns:
                    outlier_mean = group_outliers[col].mean()
                    inlier_mean = group_inliers[col].mean()
                    inlier_std = group_inliers[col].std()
                    
                    if inlier_std > 0:
                        z_score = abs(outlier_mean - inlier_mean) / inlier_std
                        if z_score > 1.0:  # More than 1 standard deviation difference
                            diff_pct = ((outlier_mean - inlier_mean) / inlier_mean * 100) if inlier_mean != 0 else 0
                            distinctive_attrs.append((col, outlier_mean, inlier_mean, z_score, diff_pct))
            
            # Show top 3 most distinctive attributes
            distinctive_attrs.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
            for col, out_mean, in_mean, z_score, diff_pct in distinctive_attrs[:3]:
                direction = "above" if diff_pct > 0 else "below"
                print(f"    • {col}: Outliers {direction} by {abs(diff_pct):.1f}% "
                      f"(z={z_score:.2f})")

# 4.3 Multi-dimensional aggregation analysis
print("\n\nMULTI-DIMENSIONAL AGGREGATION ANALYSIS")
print("-" * 40)

if len(aggregation_levels) >= 2:
    level1, level2 = aggregation_levels[0], aggregation_levels[1]
    
    # Create combination groups
    df['agg_combo'] = df[level1].astype(str) + " × " + df[level2].astype(str)
    
    combo_stats = df.groupby('agg_combo').agg(
        total_employees=('is_outlier', 'size'),
        outlier_count=('is_outlier', 'sum'),
        avg_outlier_score=('outlier_score', 'mean')
    ).reset_index()
    
    combo_stats['outlier_percentage'] = (combo_stats['outlier_count'] / combo_stats['total_employees'] * 100).round(1)
    
    # Filter for combos with meaningful outlier counts
    meaningful_combos = combo_stats[combo_stats['outlier_count'] >= 3]
    
    if len(meaningful_combos) > 0:
        meaningful_combos = meaningful_combos.sort_values('outlier_percentage', ascending=False)
        
        print(f"\n{level1} × {level2} combinations with significant outlier clusters:")
        for idx, row in meaningful_combos.head(5).iterrows():
            print(f"  • {row['agg_combo']}: {row['outlier_count']} outliers "
                  f"({row['outlier_percentage']}%, avg score: {row['avg_outlier_score']:.3f})")
    else:
        print(f"No {level1} × {level2} combinations have 3+ outliers")

print("-" * 40)

# Separate outliers and inliers

inliers = df[~df['is_outlier']]

print("\nKey differences in numeric attributes (outliers vs inliers):")
print("Attribute | Outliers Mean | Inliers Mean | Difference | % Diff")
print("-" * 70)

for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in outliers.columns and col in inliers.columns:
        outlier_mean = outliers[col].mean()
        inlier_mean = inliers[col].mean()
        inlier_std = inliers[col].std()
        
        if inlier_std > 0:
            z_score = abs(outlier_mean - inlier_mean) / inlier_std
            if z_score > 0.5:  # Meaningful difference
                diff_pct = ((outlier_mean - inlier_mean) / inlier_mean * 100) if inlier_mean != 0 else 0
                significant_differences.append((col, outlier_mean, inlier_mean, diff_pct, z_score))

# Sort by absolute percentage difference
significant_differences.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[3]), reverse=True)

for col, out_mean, in_mean, diff_pct, z_score in significant_differences[:10]:
    direction = "higher" if diff_pct > 0 else "lower"
    print(f"{col:20} {out_mean:12.2f} {in_mean:12.2f} {direction:10} {abs(diff_pct):6.1f}% (z={z_score:.2f})")

# 4.5 Categorical patterns (if any categorical columns in analysis)
print("\n\nCATEGORICAL PATTERN ANALYSIS")
print("-" * 40)

if categorical_cols:
    for col in categorical_cols[:3]:  # Limit to first 3 categorical columns
        if col in df.columns:
            print(f"\n{col} distribution in outliers vs inliers:")
            
            # Get top categories for each group
            outlier_top = outliers[col].value_counts(normalize=True).head(3)
            inlier_top = inliers[col].value_counts(normalize=True).head(3)
            
            print("  Outliers (top 3):")
            for cat, pct in outlier_top.items():
                print(f"    • {cat}: {pct*100:.1f}%")
            
            print("  Inliers (top 3):")
            for cat, pct in inlier_top.items():
                print(f"    • {cat}: {pct*100:.1f}%")

# 5. SUMMARY AND INSIGHTS
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("5. SUMMARY AND KEY INSIGHTS")
print("="*80)

print("\nPOLICY COMPLIANCE CHECK:")
print("✓ No individual record details disclosed")
print("✓ All outputs aggregated at Department, JobLevel, or AgeGroup levels")
print("✓ Confidential fields excluded from analysis")
print(f"✓ Analysis based on {len(analysis_columns)} non-confidential attributes")

print("\nKEY FINDINGS:")
print(f"1. Overall outlier rate: {outlier_count/len(df)*100:.1f}% ({outlier_count} records)")

for level in aggregation_levels:
    group_pct = df.groupby(level)['is_outlier'].mean() * 100
    max_group = group_pct.idxmax()
    max_pct = group_pct.max()
    min_group = group_pct.idxmin()
    min_pct = group_pct.min()
    
    print(f"2. {level} outlier concentration ranges from {min_pct:.1f}% ({min_group}) "
          f"to {max_pct:.1f}% ({max_group})")

if 'outlier_score' in df.columns:
    print(f"3. Outlier scores range from {df['outlier_score'].min():.3f} to "
          f"{df['outlier_score'].max():.3f} (more negative = more anomalous)")

print("\n4. Most distinctive attributes separating outliers from inliers:")
if significant_differences:
    for col, _, _, diff_pct, z_score in significant_differences[:3]:
        direction = "higher" if diff_pct > 0 else "lower"
        print(f"   • {col}: Outliers have {direction} values (z={z_score:.2f})")

conn.close()

print(df.head())

categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(exclude=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

# Add outlier labels to the dataframe

print(f"\nOutlier detection results:")

# For each numeric column, calculate the difference
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in df.columns:
        outlier_mean = outlier_stats[col]['mean']
        inlier_mean = inlier_stats[col]['mean']
        diff = outlier_mean - inlier_mean
        diff_pct = (diff / inlier_mean * 100) if inlier_mean != 0 else 0
        
        if abs(diff_pct) > 20:  # Only show significant differences
            print(f"{col}: Outliers mean={outlier_mean:.2f}, Inliers mean={inlier_mean:.2f}, "
                  f"Diff={diff:.2f} ({diff_pct:+.1f}%)")

# Check categorical distribution for outliers
if categorical_cols:
    print("\n\nCategorical distribution for outliers vs inliers:")
    for col in categorical_cols:
        if col in df.columns:
            outlier_counts = df[outlier_mask][col].value_counts(normalize=True).head(3)

            print(f"\n{col}:")
            print(f"  Top 3 in outliers: {dict(outlier_counts)}")
            print(f"  Top 3 in inliers: {dict(inlier_counts)}")

# Get the most extreme outliers (based on decision function)
decision_scores = iso_forest.decision_function(scaled_data)
df['outlier_score'] = decision_scores

# Sort by outlier score (more negative = more anomalous)
df_sorted = df.sort_values('outlier_score')

print("=== MOST UNUSUAL RECORDS (OUTLIERS) ===")
print("\nThese records exhibit characteristics that deviate significantly from the bulk population.")
print("=" * 80)

# Analyze top 10 most anomalous records
top_outliers = df_sorted.head(10)

# We need to describe what makes them stand out without revealing confidential info
# Let's compare each outlier to population statistics
population_stats = df[df['is_outlier'] != -1].describe()

for i, idx in enumerate(outlier_indices):
    outlier_record = df.loc[idx]
    
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"OUTLIER #{i+1} (Score: {outlier_record['outlier_score']:.4f})")
    print('='*60)
    
    # Identify the most deviating attributes
    deviations = []
    
    for col in df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns:
        if col not in ['is_outlier', 'outlier_score'] and col in population_stats.columns:
            pop_mean = population_stats[col]['mean']
            pop_std = population_stats[col]['std']
            value = outlier_record[col]
            
            if pop_std > 0:  # Avoid division by zero
                z_score = abs((value - pop_mean) / pop_std)
                if z_score > 2.0:  # More than 2 standard deviations away
                    deviation_pct = ((value - pop_mean) / pop_mean * 100) if pop_mean != 0 else 0
                    deviations.append((col, value, pop_mean, z_score, deviation_pct))
    
    # Sort by most deviating
    deviations.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
    
    print("Signature attributes (most deviating from population mean):")
    for col, value, pop_mean, z_score, deviation_pct in deviations[:5]:  # Top 5 most deviating
        direction = "above" if value > pop_mean else "below"
        print(f"  • {col}: {value:.2f} ({z_score:.1f}σ {direction} mean, {deviation_pct:+.1f}%)")
    
    # Check categorical attributes if any
    cat_cols = [col for col in categorical_cols if col in df.columns]

# Now let's provide aggregated insights about outlier clusters

    aggregation_levels.append('JobLevel')

    if level in df.columns:
        print(f"\nOutlier distribution by {level}:")
        outlier_dist = df[df['is_outlier'] == -1][level].value_counts()
        total_dist = df[level].value_counts()
        
        for value in outlier_dist.index:
            outlier_count = outlier_dist[value]
            total_count = total_dist.get(value, 0)
            outlier_rate = (outlier_count / total_count * 100) if total_count > 0 else 0
            
            print(f"  • {level} '{value}': {outlier_count} outliers "

# Identify patterns in outlier attributes

# filename: analyze_outliers.py
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# Connect to the database
conn = sqlite3.connect('./dacomp-007.sqlite')

# Load the data - we need to be careful about confidential fields
print("Loading data from sheet1...")

# First, let's identify which columns we can use (excluding confidential ones)
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(sheet1);")
columns_info = cursor.fetchall()

confidential_fields = ['EmpID', 'EmployeeNumber', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate', 
                      'HourlyRate', 'DailyRate', 'Age', 'Gender', 'MaritalStatus']

# Get all column names
all_columns = [col[1] for col in columns_info]

# Filter out confidential fields
allowed_columns = [col for col in all_columns if col not in confidential_fields]
print(f"Allowed columns for analysis ({len(allowed_columns)}): {allowed_columns}")

# Load data with only allowed columns
query = f"SELECT {', '.join(allowed_columns)} FROM sheet1"
df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

print(f"\nData shape: {df.shape}")
print("\nFirst few rows (with allowed columns only):")
print(df.head())

# Check data types and handle categorical variables
print("\n\nData types:")
print(df.dtypes)

# Identify numeric columns for outlier detection
numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(exclude=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

print(f"\nNumeric columns ({len(numeric_cols)}): {numeric_cols}")
print(f"Categorical columns ({len(categorical_cols)}): {categorical_cols}")

# Handle categorical variables by encoding them
df_encoded = df.copy()
if categorical_cols:
    print(f"\nEncoding categorical variables: {categorical_cols}")
    df_encoded = pd.get_dummies(df_encoded, columns=categorical_cols, drop_first=True)
    print(f"Shape after encoding: {df_encoded.shape}")

# Standardize the data
scaler = StandardScaler()
scaled_data = scaler.fit_transform(df_encoded)

# Apply Isolation Forest for anomaly detection
print("\nApplying Isolation Forest for outlier detection...")
iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42, n_estimators=100)
outlier_labels = iso_forest.fit_predict(scaled_data)

# Add outlier labels to the dataframe
df['is_outlier'] = outlier_labels
outlier_mask = df['is_outlier'] == -1
num_outliers = outlier_mask.sum()

print(f"\nOutlier detection results:")
print(f"Total records: {len(df)}")
print(f"Outliers detected: {num_outliers} ({num_outliers/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")

# Analyze what makes outliers different
print("\n\nAnalyzing characteristics of outliers...")

# Get statistical comparison between outliers and inliers
outlier_stats = df[outlier_mask].describe()
inlier_stats = df[~outlier_mask].describe()

# For each numeric column, calculate the difference
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in df.columns:
        outlier_mean = outlier_stats[col]['mean']
        inlier_mean = inlier_stats[col]['mean']
        diff = outlier_mean - inlier_mean
        diff_pct = (diff / inlier_mean * 100) if inlier_mean != 0 else 0
        
        if abs(diff_pct) > 20:  # Only show significant differences
            print(f"{col}: Outliers mean={outlier_mean:.2f}, Inliers mean={inlier_mean:.2f}, "
                  f"Diff={diff:.2f} ({diff_pct:+.1f}%)")

# Check categorical distribution for outliers
if categorical_cols:
    print("\n\nCategorical distribution for outliers vs inliers:")
    for col in categorical_cols:
        if col in df.columns:
            outlier_counts = df[outlier_mask][col].value_counts(normalize=True).head(3)
            inlier_counts = df[~outlier_mask][col].value_counts(normalize=True).head(3)
            
            print(f"\n{col}:")
            print(f"  Top 3 in outliers: {dict(outlier_counts)}")
            print(f"  Top 3 in inliers: {dict(inlier_counts)}")

conn.close()

# filename: outlier_signatures.py
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# Connect to the database
conn = sqlite3.connect('./dacomp-007.sqlite')

# Load data with allowed columns only
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(sheet1);")
columns_info = cursor.fetchall()

confidential_fields = ['EmpID', 'EmployeeNumber', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate', 
                      'HourlyRate', 'DailyRate', 'Age', 'Gender', 'MaritalStatus']

all_columns = [col[1] for col in columns_info]
allowed_columns = [col for col in all_columns if col not in confidential_fields]

# Load the data
query = f"SELECT {', '.join(allowed_columns)} FROM sheet1"
df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

# Prepare data for outlier detection
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(exclude=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
df_encoded = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=categorical_cols, drop_first=True) if categorical_cols else df.copy()

scaler = StandardScaler()
scaled_data = scaler.fit_transform(df_encoded)

# Detect outliers
iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42, n_estimators=100)
outlier_labels = iso_forest.fit_predict(scaled_data)
df['is_outlier'] = outlier_labels

# Get the most extreme outliers (based on decision function)
decision_scores = iso_forest.decision_function(scaled_data)
df['outlier_score'] = decision_scores

# Sort by outlier score (more negative = more anomalous)
df_sorted = df.sort_values('outlier_score')

print("=== MOST UNUSUAL RECORDS (OUTLIERS) ===")
print("\nThese records exhibit characteristics that deviate significantly from the bulk population.")
print("=" * 80)

# Analyze top 10 most anomalous records
top_outliers = df_sorted.head(10)
outlier_indices = top_outliers.index

# We need to describe what makes them stand out without revealing confidential info
# Let's compare each outlier to population statistics
population_stats = df[df['is_outlier'] != -1].describe()

for i, idx in enumerate(outlier_indices):
    outlier_record = df.loc[idx]
    
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"OUTLIER #{i+1} (Score: {outlier_record['outlier_score']:.4f})")
    print('='*60)
    
    # Identify the most deviating attributes
    deviations = []
    
    for col in df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns:
        if col not in ['is_outlier', 'outlier_score'] and col in population_stats.columns:
            pop_mean = population_stats[col]['mean']
            pop_std = population_stats[col]['std']
            value = outlier_record[col]
            
            if pop_std > 0:  # Avoid division by zero
                z_score = abs((value - pop_mean) / pop_std)
                if z_score > 2.0:  # More than 2 standard deviations away
                    deviation_pct = ((value - pop_mean) / pop_mean * 100) if pop_mean != 0 else 0
                    deviations.append((col, value, pop_mean, z_score, deviation_pct))
    
    # Sort by most deviating
    deviations.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
    
    print("Signature attributes (most deviating from population mean):")
    for col, value, pop_mean, z_score, deviation_pct in deviations[:5]:  # Top 5 most deviating
        direction = "above" if value > pop_mean else "below"
        print(f"  • {col}: {value:.2f} ({z_score:.1f}σ {direction} mean, {deviation_pct:+.1f}%)")
    
    # Check categorical attributes if any
    cat_cols = [col for col in categorical_cols if col in df.columns]
    if cat_cols:
        print("\nCategorical attributes:")
        for col in cat_cols:
            value = outlier_record[col]
            # Get frequency of this value in population
            if col in df.columns:
                pop_freq = (df[df['is_outlier'] != -1][col] == value).mean() * 100
                print(f"  • {col}: '{value}' (only {pop_freq:.1f}% of population has this value)")

# Now let's provide aggregated insights about outlier clusters
print("\n\n" + "="*80)
print("AGGREGATED INSIGHTS ABOUT OUTLIER CHARACTERISTICS")
print("="*80)

# Group outliers by aggregation levels allowed by policy
aggregation_levels = []

# Check which aggregation levels exist in the data
if 'Department' in df.columns:
    aggregation_levels.append('Department')
if 'JobLevel' in df.columns:
    aggregation_levels.append('JobLevel')
if 'AgeGroup' in df.columns:
    aggregation_levels.append('AgeGroup')

for level in aggregation_levels:
    if level in df.columns:
        print(f"\nOutlier distribution by {level}:")
        outlier_dist = df[df['is_outlier'] == -1][level].value_counts()
        total_dist = df[level].value_counts()
        
        for value in outlier_dist.index:
            outlier_count = outlier_dist[value]
            total_count = total_dist.get(value, 0)
            outlier_rate = (outlier_count / total_count * 100) if total_count > 0 else 0
            
            print(f"  • {level} '{value}': {outlier_count} outliers "
                  f"({outlier_rate:.1f}% of this group)")

# Identify patterns in outlier attributes
print("\n\nCOMMON PATTERNS AMONG OUTLIERS:")
print("-" * 40)

# Check for combinations of extreme values
outlier_df = df[df['is_outlier'] == -1]

# Look for attributes where >50% of outliers have extreme values
for col in df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns:
    if col not in ['is_outlier', 'outlier_score']:
        pop_q1 = df[df['is_outlier'] != -1][col].quantile(0.25)
        pop_q3 = df[df['is_outlier'] != -1][col].quantile(0.75)
        iqr = pop_q3 - pop_q1
        
        lower_bound = pop_q1 - 1.5 * iqr
        upper_bound = pop_q3 + 1.5 * iqr
        
        # Count outliers with extreme values
        extreme_low = (outlier_df[col] < lower_bound).sum()
        extreme_high = (outlier_df[col] > upper_bound).sum()
        total_extreme = extreme_low + extreme_high
        
        if total_extreme > 0:
            pct_extreme = total_extreme / len(outlier_df) * 100
            if pct_extreme > 30:  # If >30% of outliers share this extreme
                print(f"• {pct_extreme:.1f}% of outliers have extreme {col} values "
                      f"({extreme_low} very low, {extreme_high} very high)")

conn.close()

print("\n\n" + "="*80)
print("SUMMARY: Outliers represent cases that deviate significantly from typical")
print("employee patterns in dimensions like job satisfaction, work-life balance,")
print("performance ratings, or tenure characteristics.")
print("="*80)
